GATE 2/3 — `rebar review-code` on Bedrock: PASS. Recorded immediately on completion, before any
aggregation, because the previous attempt at this gate completed its five calls and then died while
writing the record — the calls were billed and produced nothing durable.

  command   rebar review-code   (REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE=~/.config/rebar/bedrock.toml)
  exit      0
  usage log $CLAUDE_JOB_DIR/tmp/usage_1aa2_gate2.jsonl  (durable path, survives process death)

PER-CALL MODEL TALLY — 5 calls, ALL on Bedrock inference profiles:
    3 x bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8      (frontier)
    2 x bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6    (standard)
  NON-BEDROCK CALLS: 0    <- the provider-clean criterion, satisfied

CACHE — the criterion is nonzero cache_READ, not merely write, because write-only is exactly bug
f81d's failure mode:
    cache_read_tokens   18,292      <- nonzero, so caching is genuinely ENGAGING on the Bedrock path
    cache_write_tokens  10,571
    input_tokens       240,483

So on the Bedrock path a real code-review gate parses its verdict, resolves both the frontier and
standard classes to inference profiles, makes zero direct-Anthropic calls, and reads from cache rather
than only writing to it.

METHOD NOTE, since this is the fourth attempt at this gate: it was run as a detached background job
rather than inside an agent. Four consecutive agent attempts were killed by the 600s stream watchdog —
live gate runs on this loaded host exceed that window, so the failure was structural rather than bad
luck. A background job has no watchdog. Combined with the durable usage-log path, evidence now survives
a process death instead of being re-bought.
